small_guidance: The output mismatch is likely from TritonLinear: weight.t().contiguous() is recomputed every forward but more importantly the lm_head in GPT2 shares weights with wte (embedding); replacing it with TritonLinear that stores a transposed copy can desync. Fix by either (a) keeping lm_head on PyTorch, or (b) computing w_t from self.weight on each call without caching, and ensure dtype/device match. Also verify fused_layernorm handles N=768 with BLOCK_SIZE=1024 correctly (mask works). Add a correctness check by comparing one layer's output against F.layer_norm and F.linear before integrating.
large_guidance: Redesign the module replacement to be safer: (1) skip replacing tied-weight lm_head (GPT2's lm_head shares wte.weight) — leave it as PyTorch or implement it as an explicit matmul against wte.weight without transposing/caching; (2) write a single autotuned matmul kernel that supports an optional transpose flag for B (so Linear can pass weight without materializing weight.t()); (3) keep LayerNorm and GELU fused but verify against F.layer_norm with the exact eps used by HF (1e-5). Consider a single-pass Welford LayerNorm to reduce loads from 3N to N.
